newsitem.title: USA: OTR Express sees freight demand improving.
newsitem.headline: OTR Express sees freight demand improving.

text.p: OTR Express Inc., a long-haul truckload carrier, said demand for freight services is improving and a national over-capacity of trucks is being alleviated by lower sales of new trucks.

"The trends for our freight statistics are very positive during the past six months, which reflects stronger freight markets as well as a contribution from our new marketing program," William Ward, president and CEO, said in a statement.
"We set out to reduce our reliance on freight brokers, which offer lower revenue rates than direct shippers," Ward added.
"As of mid-October we have increased our percentage of freight obtained from shippers to 71 percent from 47 percent at the beginning of the year," Ward added.
OTR Express also said it plans to expand its fleet by 50 units in 1997 from the current level of 503 units due to improving freight market conditions.
In addition, the company said it will purchase 150 new tractors as replacement units in 1997.

The company also announced plans to continue an upgrade of the trailer fleet from 48-foot trailers to 53-foot trailers with air-ride suspension. The company said it will purchase 240 new 53-foot trailers in 1997, including 50 expansion units and 190 replacement units.
The program will result in conversion of 67 percent of the fleet to 53-foot trailers by the end of 1997.
Ward said diesel fuel prices, which have been higher than normal throughout 1996, have reached a new high for the year.

The company said its blended average fuel cost is currently $1.27 a gallon compared to normal pricing levels of $1.00 to $1.10 a gallon. The company said it is recovering a large percentage of the additional fuel cost through fuel surcharges to customers as well as its fuel hedging program.
